svg.title: DDIA 1 · RELIABLE, SCALABLE, MAINTAINABLE: sketchnote
svg.text: The three words every NFR discussion comes back to.
A failure is when the whole system stops serving users. You
design so faults don't become failures.
Reads become one cache lookup. The cost moved to write
The user waits for the slowest backend. With 100 backends at
1% slow each, 63% of user requests hit at least one slow call.
SCALING UP VS SCALING OUT, AND
When one box is not enough
There is no "magic scaling sauce". An architecture for 100k
req/sec of 1KB reads looks nothing like one for 3 req/min
Name the load parameter (reads/sec, fan-out, data size), calculate it, then say which component breaks first.
p99 < 200ms for reads, not averages. Mention tail amplification if requests fan out.
Separate fault from failure: "A node dying is a fault. Replicas plus health checks mean it never becomes a
"Before choosing components, let me pin down the load parameters: DAU, read:write ratio, and peak
QPS, because they decide whether we need any distribution at all."
Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann). Read the book.
